title: Judith Beheading Holofernes
museum: Gallerie Nazionali Barberini Corsini, Palazzo Barberini
alt: Judith draws a sword across a man's neck while an older woman waits beside them against a dark ground and red curtain.
note: The Palazzo Barberini painting shows Judith, Holofernes and an older attendant. The museum's catalogue dates it about 1599.
featureReviewReason: A compact naturalistic group performs a visible attack. Strong gestures and selective light dominate, while dark ground and drapery provide little setting.

title: The Supper at Emmaus
commonsTitle: File:1602-3 Caravaggio,Supper at Emmaus National Gallery, London.jpg
alt: Four men gather at a table of food, with one seated man extending both arms and another pushing back from his chair.
note: Caravaggio painted this London version in 1601 and another version in Milan in 1606. The London museum record supplies the date used here.
featureReviewReason: Naturalistic figures gesture around a table crowded with food and objects. The plain rear wall limits setting despite the strong light and bodily movement.

title: The Taking of Christ
museum: National Gallery of Ireland, on loan from the Jesuit Community, Leeson Street
alt: A tightly packed group surrounds Christ, with a kissing figure, armoured soldiers, raised hands and a lantern against darkness.
note: The National Gallery of Ireland identifies this as the 1602 painting on indefinite loan from the Jesuit Community in Dublin.
featureReviewReason: Interlocked foreground bodies, grasping hands and a lantern dominate. The compressed scene provides almost no surrounding place.

title: The Triumph of Death
commonsTitle: File:The Triumph of Death by Pieter Bruegel the Elder.jpg
alt: An army of skeletons overwhelms people across a crowded landscape of fires, bodies, carts and distant ships.
note: Bruegel distributes many encounters across one broad landscape. This is the Prado painting by Pieter Bruegel the Elder, rather than a later version by his sons.
featureReviewReason: Many small physical encounters and objects fill a deep landscape. Density and visible action are scored separately from any viewer feeling about the subject.

title: The Spinners, or The Fable of Arachne
commonsTitle: File:Velázquez - La Fábula de Aracne o Las Hilanderas (Museo del Prado, 1657-58).jpg
alt: Women work with wool and a spinning wheel in a shadowed foreground while another group stands before a tapestry in a brighter rear space.
note: Foreground work and a second scene occupy different spatial stages. The canvas has later edge additions; the selected reproduction is retained consistently without a new crop.
featureReviewReason: Visible work in the foreground and a smaller rear scene occupy separate spatial stages within a detailed room.

title: The Arnolfini Portrait
alt: A richly dressed pair stand in a furnished room with a small dog, chandelier, red bed and a round mirror reflecting the doorway.
note: The painting's mirror reflects additional figures beyond the pictured couple. The National Gallery cautions that the woman's gathered dress is not evidence of pregnancy.
featureReviewReason: The pair hold restrained poses, while the mirror, furnishings, dog and other objects create dense detail within a coherent room.

title: Luncheon of the Boating Party
commonsTitle: File:Pierre-Auguste Renoir - Luncheon of the Boating Party - Google Art Project.jpg
alt: A group eat, drink and talk around a crowded table beneath a striped awning beside a riverside railing.
note: Renoir combines a social gathering, table objects and a riverside setting. The Phillips Collection dates the painting between 1880 and 1881.
featureReviewReason: Numerous people drink, converse and gesture around table objects within a bright riverside social setting.

title: Animal Destinies (Tierschicksale)
alt: Animals and trees overlap within sharp red, blue, green and brown planes that fracture the surrounding forest.
note: The work is also known in English as Fate of the Animals. Its fragmented forms retain recognisable animals and trees rather than becoming fully nonfigurative.
featureReviewReason: Angular saturated planes fracture recognisable animals and trees. Animal movement and the forest remain visible; no human figures are depicted.
